title: Content revision: drop the Git-filter refusal, which only costs filter-configured repositories their basis
outcome:
Candidate from Opus's review of tm-5gi4 phase 1 (landed as acd7740).

content_revision goes through ReviewFreezeGit::new, which refuses a repository that configures Git filters. The code says so itself (src/content_revision.rs:65-67): nothing in a content revision runs a filter, because ls-files runs none and files are read from the worktree. The refusal is kept for uniformity with the freeze, not for safety. A repository with a repo-level filter config, such as Git LFS installed locally, therefore gets no basis for no reason.

Fix: let content_revision construct its pinned Git without the filter refusal (the freeze keeps its own), and add a test for a repository with a filter.<name>.clean config that still gets a revision.
disposal_reason: Duplicate found in backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 3b; Termal::Fable2). The Git-filter refusal (an LFS repository loses its basis) is covered by w-c07c410dac75, which covers both submodules and Git filters or LFS for the team pilot.
